title: Turing mechanisms in a multimode open quantum system
authors: Giorgia Comparato, Francesco Gargano, Rosario Lo Franco
abstract: We investigate pattern formation in a finite chain of bosonic modes whose dynamics is governed by a Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equation. The model combines local parametric driving and nonlinear damping with nonlocal dissipative couplings between modes that work on different discrete spatial scales. In the classical limit, these mechanisms generate a reaction-diffusion-like dynamics, allowing the emergence of Turing-type instabilities. The key aspect of the analysis is the coexistence and competition of different unstable spatial modes. Depending on the range of parameters, the system may select different stationary nonuniform configurations, oscillatory wave-like states, or regimes in which multiple modes interact before a dominant pattern is established, thus providing a mechanism for pattern selection. We compare the deterministic bifurcation scenario, generated by a reaction-diffusion-like system derived from semiclassical drift dynamics, with the quantum dynamics, derived via the GKSL master equation, using phase-space methods and reduced Wigner functions. The results show how Turing instabilities, mode competition, and pattern selection can be extended to multimode open quantum systems, providing a bridge between nonlinear dynamical systems, dissipative quantum mechanics, and spatial self-organization.
summary: This paper analyzes pattern formation in an open quantum system modeled as a bosonic chain subject to local and nonlocal dissipation. By deriving mean-field equations from the GKSL master equation, the authors show that Turing instabilities can emerge, allowing for the selection of stable spatial patterns. This connects nonlinear dynamics theory with dissipative quantum mechanics.
main_problem: The study investigates pattern formation, specifically Turing instabilities, within a multimode open quantum system.
main_result: The analysis successfully extends the concept of Turing instability and mode competition to open quantum systems, showing that spatial self-organization can emerge from dissipative quantum dynamics.
method: The approach involves deriving mean-field equations for field amplitudes ($\langle \hat{a}_j angle$) from the full GKSL master equation, followed by linear stability analysis of these resulting reaction-diffusion-like systems.
model_or_system: The system is a finite chain of bosonic modes (at least three sites) whose dynamics are governed by a GKSL master equation incorporating local parametric driving and both short-range ($\lambda$) and long-range ($\kappa$) nonlinear dissipative couplings.
key_observables: Field amplitudes ($\alpha_j$), reduced Wigner functions, and the stability eigenvalues of the linearized system.
important_parameters: Nonlocal coupling strengths ($\lambda, \kappa$), detuning ($\Delta$), and parametric drive ($\eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on deriving a semiclassical mean-field approximation from the full quantum master equation; comparisons are made between this deterministic limit and the full quantum evolution.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the complex open quantum system dynamics via the GKSL master equation, deriving the corresponding reaction-diffusion mean-field equations, performing linear stability analysis to identify Turing instability conditions, and finally comparing these deterministic results with full quantum simulations using Wigner functions.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial theoretical bridge by demonstrating how classical pattern formation mechanisms (Turing instabilities) can be rigorously mapped onto the dynamics of open quantum systems, which is highly relevant for understanding dissipative quantum matter.
